lens: Is the inference sound as statistics — multiplicity, effect sizes and intervals, group construction in the code, independence, the n actually used, and whether the analysis could have returned a null?
what_i_read: research/modalities/emc_expression_panels.py (scoring, verdict, concordance state machine, genome-wide null)
central_claim: Of five therapeutic classes selected on a molecular state rather than a histology, public transcript data from 16 archival EMC tumours on two array platforms shows the selecting state is absent for four; the fifth (BH3-mimetics) survives because the instrument cannot reach the question. The paper's stated methodological claim is that grading how strong each negative is, separately, is the whole contribution.

blockers.summary: Seven of the 42 samples in GSE24369 fall into NO group and are silently dropped; five of them are Solitary fibrous tumour, a sarcoma that belongs in the comparator arm the paper defines as '29 comparator sarcomas'.
blockers.evidence: emc-expression-panels.json -> platforms['GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz']: n_samples = 42, but class_counts = {EMC: 6, LGFMS: 17, desmoid_fibromatosis: 6, fibrosarcoma: 6, unclassified: 7} and n_comparator = 29. The seven unclassified rows, read verbatim from sample_annotations_verbatim, are GSM600963-GSM600967 ('Solitary fibrous tumor 1..5') and GSM600968-GSM600969 ('Skeletal muscle pooled RNA 1..2'). The two pooled-RNA rows are correctly not tumours. The five solitary fibrous tumours are soft-tissue sarcoma biopsies on the same array, in the same series, annotated 'sample type: tumor biopsy' exactly like every included comparator. They fall out only because the sample classifier is string matching (artifact _limits: 'SAMPLE CLASSIFICATION IS STRING MATCHING on the verbatim GEO annotation, reused from emc_atr_vulnerability._classify_sample') and no rule matches 'Solitary fibrous tumor'. The paper's section 1 table prints '29 comparator sarcomas' and nowhere states that the series holds 42 samples or that 5 sarcomas were excluded; no exclusion rule is printed anywhere in the manuscript. Every t in section 2 of the paper is computed against this silently truncated arm, and the direction and size of the change from adding 5 more comparators is unknown and not bounded anywhere.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Either (a) print the full sample accounting in section 1 — 42 samples, 6 EMC, 29 comparators, 5 solitary fibrous tumours and 2 pooled skeletal-muscle references excluded, with the exclusion rule stated as a rule rather than as the output of an unstated string match — and state that the SFT exclusion is an artefact of the classifier rather than a design choice; or (b) re-run with SFT in the comparator arm and report both. Without one of these the reader cannot tell that a comparison group was defined by what a regex happened to match.

blockers.summary: The paper's one class-keeping-open inference rests on a cross-platform concordance claim for NOXA where one of the two platforms reads t = 0.628, with 76% of that array's genes at least as extreme — and the paper prints no statistic for it at all, while printing t for every group score around it.
blockers.evidence: Paper section 2.5: 'NOXA — the BH3-only protein that specifically neutralises MCL-1 — is HIGHER in EMC on both platforms, and on GPL3290 by 1.74 standard deviations of that array', which then carries 'Low guardians with a high sensitiser is the transcriptional shadow of a primed cell... This is the one class of the five that stays open.' In emc-expression-panels.json, NOXA is PMAIP1. GSE24369/GPL6244: EMC mean_z 0.3073 vs comparator 0.0781, a difference of 0.229 SD units; its own genome_wide_null placement on that platform is t = 0.628, signed_percentile 64.53, frac_of_array_at_least_as_extreme_two_sided = 0.76178, n_symbols_at_least_as_extreme = 14243 of 18697. GSE4303/GPL3290: EMC -0.2219 vs comparator -1.9659 (difference 1.744, matching the paper's 1.74), t = 7.593, 66 of 14403 symbols at least as extreme. So the claim is one very strong platform and one platform that is statistically indistinguishable from the array background. The artifact's own _limits state the standard the paper is failing here: 'Concordance across the two is the argument; a single-platform result is a lead.' Every group-level result in the paper carries its t in parentheses (t = -4.57, -2.54, 2.42, 2.23, -0.19, 0.16, -2.20, -1.13, -0.22, 1.71, -1.02, -0.08, -0.57, 1.04); the one reading where the t is 0.628 is the one reading printed without a t.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Print NOXA's statistic on both platforms as it is printed for everything else — e.g. 'higher in EMC on GPL3290 by 1.74 SD (t = 7.59) and directionally higher but not distinguishable from background on GPL6244 (0.23 SD, t = 0.63, 76% of that array's genes at least as extreme)' — and reword 'HIGHER in EMC on both platforms' so it no longer asserts concordance the data does not carry. If the primed-cell reading survives that honest statement, it survives; as written the sentence borrows strength from a platform that supplies none.

blockers.summary: The artifact computed a genome-wide empirical null for exactly this statistic, and it shows the nominal Welch t the paper prints is anticonservative by roughly a factor of two in |t| and an order of magnitude in p. Read against that null, every t the paper uses as evidence of a PRESENT effect sits where a quarter to a third of the whole array sits.
blockers.evidence: emc-expression-panels.json -> platforms[*].genome_wide_null, described in the artifact as 'Welch t, EMC vs comparator, for EVERY symbol this platform's probes map to - the distribution a panel gene's own t has to be read against', computed with 'Identical arithmetic to gene_reads'. GPL6244 (18,697 symbols) t percentiles: p05 -4.207, p50 -0.147, p95 3.495. GPL3290 (14,403 symbols): p05 -3.138, p50 0.191, p95 3.851. A correctly calibrated Welch t at these df (6-16) would put p05/p95 near -1.8/+1.8. Recomputing the empirical two-sided tail from the placed_wanted_genes records: on GPL6244 empirical p = 0.05 is reached only at |t| ~ 4.89 and p = 0.10 at |t| ~ 3.85; on GPL3290 p = 0.05 at |t| ~ 4.40 and p = 0.10 at |t| ~ 3.52. The 87 (GPL6244) and 82 (GPL3290) placed genes with |t| in [2.1, 2.3] carry empirical two-sided p of 0.288-0.325 and 0.256-0.294 respectively. Consequences for the paper's printed statistics: the alt-EJ elevation in section 2.4 (t = 2.42 and 2.23), presented as a real cross-platform observation that 'nothing in the literature explains', is at empirical p ~ 0.29 and ~ 0.26 - roughly one array gene in four moves at least that hard. ASS1, the 'strongest of the four negatives', is at empirical p 0.069 (1,290 of 18,697 symbols at least as extreme) and 0.046 (669 of 14,403). Only the guardian-abundance read on GPL6244 (t = -4.57) approaches the empirical 0.05 line. This is NOT the 'uncorrected for multiple testing' caveat the paper prints in sections 3 and 5: correction assumes the reference distribution is right. Here the reference distribution is wrong, and no Bonferroni or FDR applied to a miscalibrated t recovers it. Cross-check that the group statistic is not better behaved than the per-gene one: across all 156 group x platform scores emitted in the artifact, 60 (38.5%) have |t| >= 2.20, versus ~26-29% of individual symbols in the genome-wide null - the group score is if anything more inflated, not less.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Place every quoted t against the genome-wide null the artifact already holds - i.e. report frac_of_array_at_least_as_extreme_two_sided beside each t - and rewrite any sentence whose force depends on a |t| near 2 being meaningful. Sections 3 and 5 must stop describing the problem as 'uncorrected for multiple testing' and state that the panel t is read against an empirical array-wide null in which |t| = 2.2 is unremarkable. Note this cuts BOTH ways and should be said so: it strengthens the four negatives (a flat read is even less likely to be hiding an effect) and it removes the evidential basis for the two POSITIVE readings the paper reports - the alt-EJ elevation and the NOXA elevation.

blockers.summary: The paper defers its proliferation/cellularity falsifier (F8) to a future series, but the proliferation control is already computed in the artifact it cites, and on GPL3290 it does NOT come back clean - MKI67 is higher in EMC by 1.24 SD, in the same direction as every GPL3290 result the paper treats as a finding.
blockers.evidence: Paper section 4, F8: 'none of these readings is a proliferation or cellularity artefact' - killed by 'a series matched on proliferation in which the contrasts disappear'. emc-expression-panels.json -> panels.instrument_controls states the design intent verbatim: 'MKI67: approximately FLAT in GSE24369. EMC is slow-cycling; a large proliferation delta would say the contrast is being driven by cellularity.' gene_reads.MKI67: GSE24369/GPL6244 delta_a_minus_b = +0.129, t = 0.528 (flat, as designed). GSE4303/GPL3290 delta_a_minus_b = +1.2358, t = 2.301, signed_percentile 84.58 - i.e. the proliferation reference is HIGHER in EMC by 1.24 SD units of that array. That is larger in magnitude than every GPL3290 effect the paper quotes: the alt-EJ module elevation (+0.2578 SD), the guardian depression (-0.4097 SD), the p53 output depression (-0.1416 SD), and comparable to the flagship NOXA elevation (+1.744 SD). The artifact wrote the flatness expectation for GSE24369 only, so the control was never stated for the platform where it fails. Direction matters: on GPL3290 the readings the paper treats as positive findings (ASS1 +1.55, NOXA +1.744, alt-EJ +0.2578) all share a sign with a proliferation reference that moves +1.24 SD, while the one reading that goes the other way (guardians, -0.41) is the one the paper calls clean. The paper presents F8 as an open question needing new data; the check exists, is free, is in the cited artifact, and half of it fails.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Report the MKI67 control for both platforms in section 1, state that it is flat on GPL6244 (t = 0.53) and not flat on GPL3290 (+1.24 SD, t = 2.30), and re-grade every GPL3290-dependent claim with that confound stated. F8 must stop reading as an unaddressed future test and start reading as a control that was run and passed on one platform only.

p1s.summary: POLQ - the transcript for the target of the class section 2.4 is about - is unreadable on GPL3290 and essentially flat on GPL6244; the 'alt-EJ half IS present, concordantly' claim is carried entirely by the XRCC1-LIG3-PARP1 single-strand-break-repair trio, and the paper discloses neither fact.
p1s.evidence: emc-expression-panels.json panels.ddr_mmej.groups.alt_ej_module: genes_requested = [POLQ, LIG3, PARP1, XRCC1]. On GSE24369/GPL6244 all four are readable; on GSE4303/GPL3290 genes_not_readable = ['POLQ'], so the module scored there is {LIG3, PARP1, XRCC1}. gene_reads.POLQ on GPL6244: delta_a_minus_b = +0.0446 SD, t = 0.309, and its genome_wide_null placement is frac_of_array_at_least_as_extreme_two_sided = 0.8803 - 16,459 of 18,697 symbols on that array move at least as hard. Member t values (with empirical two-sided p from the artifact's own null): GPL6244 LIG3 1.328 (0.517), PARP1 1.241 (0.545), XRCC1 2.457 (0.262); GPL3290 LIG3 2.085 (0.296), PARP1 1.524 (0.433), XRCC1 0.687 (0.717). Not one member is distinguishable from its array's background. The paper's sentence 'every readable member is higher on both' is literally true of sign and says nothing about magnitude; the sentence 'the alt-EJ module is higher in EMC on both platforms' compares two different gene sets, and the set common to both is the XRCC1-LIG3-PARP1 complex, which is single-strand-break repair rather than the Pol-theta pathway the class targets.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: State in section 2.4 that POLQ has no probe on GPL3290 and is flat on GPL6244 (t = 0.31, 88% of the array at least as extreme), that the two platforms therefore score different modules, and that the cross-platform part of the observation rests on LIG3/PARP1/XRCC1. Then re-word 'concordantly' and remove or heavily qualify 'a reader deciding whether to spend a sequencing run on this disease should have it'.

p1s.summary: Within the pre-defined five-member sensitiser group, the paper reports the one member that moves the way its argument needs and suppresses both the group score and the two members that move the opposite way at larger |t|.
p1s.evidence: emc-expression-panels.json panels.apoptotic_dependency.groups.bh3_only_sensitisers: genes_requested = [BCL2L11, PMAIP1, BID, BAD, BIK]; group score GPL6244 t = -0.168 (LOWER in EMC), GPL3290 t = 2.16 (HIGHER) - discordant, and neither figure appears in the paper. Members on GPL6244: BCL2L11 t = -2.575, BIK t = -2.105, BAD t = 0.619, BID t = 1.789, PMAIP1 t = 0.628. The paper reports PMAIP1 (NOXA) alone. The contrast with the paper's own handling of the adjacent group is the tell: for the guardians the paper reports the GROUP statistic (t = -4.57, -2.54); for the sensitisers it reports a single member. Both groups were curated in the same artifact, in the same panel, at the same time.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Report the sensitiser group score on both platforms alongside the guardian group score, and state that NOXA is one of five members and that two others move the other way on GPL6244. If NOXA is singled out on mechanistic grounds (it is the MCL-1-specific sensitiser), say that is a pre-specified mechanistic choice and not a result of the reading.

p1s.summary: n is stated once, as a series-level pair, and is not the n the code used for several quoted figures - including the paper's flagship NOXA number.
p1s.evidence: Paper section 1 table prints GSE4303 as 10 EMC / 6 comparator, and section 5 as 'Sixteen tumours'. Across the 61 genes in the paper's five panels, gene_reads on GPL3290 gives n_EMC in {4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10} and n_comparator in {2, 3, 4, 5, 6}; 11 of the 56 readable genes use fewer than 6 comparators and 8 use fewer than 10 EMC. Specifically: PMAIP1 (NOXA, the '1.74 standard deviations' figure) is 10 vs 5; RAD51 is 8 vs 3 and PALB2 10 vs 4 inside the homologous-recombination arm that carries the section 2.4 exclusion; EED is 9 vs 6 inside the PRC2 group. No n appears anywhere in section 2 of the paper. GPL6244 is clean by contrast (6 vs 29 for all 59 readable genes).
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Print n beside every gene-level figure quoted, or add one sentence to section 1 stating that on GPL3290 per-gene n falls as low as 10 vs 5 for quoted single-gene readings because some samples carry no value for some probes.

p1s.summary: The paper contains no interval anywhere, and reports test statistics without the effect sizes the artifact holds - the inverse of the usual defect, and it leaves every 'flat' and 'near a floor' judgement as an unstated cut-off.
p1s.evidence: Search of the manuscript: no confidence interval, no standard error, no p-value, and no bootstrap or replicate spread appears in any of its 2,033 words. Fourteen t values are printed; the corresponding delta_a_minus_b effect sizes in emc-expression-panels.json are never printed (e.g. the guardians are lower by 0.259 and 0.410 SD units, the alt-EJ module higher by 0.087 and 0.258 SD units, the p53 output lower by 0.180 and 0.142 SD units - all absent from the paper). Only two effect sizes appear at all: NOXA's '1.74 standard deviations' and ASS1's '92nd percentile' (artifact EMC mean_array_percentile 0.9152 - verified). Meanwhile the verbal thresholds the paper applies are never numerically defined: 'flat', 'mildly higher', 'anywhere near a floor'. The generating code does define one - emc_expression_panels.py line 1974, `strength = ("|t| >= 3" if abs(t) >= 3 else "|t| 2-3" if abs(t) >= 2 else "|t| < 2 - flat")`, and the concordance state machine at lines ~2318-2330 uses the same |t| >= 2 cut to call CONCORDANT_UP_ON_BOTH vs FLAT_ON_BOTH. That |t| = 2 cut-off governs every 'flat' in the paper and is printed nowhere in it; the artifact itself warns 'A |t| threshold in a verdict sentence is a readability aid, not a test.'
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Print delta (SD units) beside every t, and state the |t| = 2 convention explicitly as the convention it is - together with the genome-wide-null finding above, which is what tells the reader what that convention is actually worth.

p1s.summary: The five classes were chosen from sixteen routes graded against readings that already existed, and the paper presents the selection as if five questions had been asked.
p1s.evidence: census-route-expression-grading.json grades 16 routes (RT-ARGININE, RT-RET, RT-HYPOXIA-PRODRUG, RT-MATRIX-SYNTHESIS, RT-ALK-HIT, RT-MATRIX-ADDRESS, RT-IMMUNOCYTOKINE, RT-NR2F1, RT-MTAP-PRMT5, RT-TXN-CDK, RT-CHAPERONE, RT-APOPTOSIS-DEP, RT-MDM2, RT-EZH2, RT-SGK1, RT-POLQ) and states in its own header: 'The census registered these routes on 2026-08-09 with a cheapest next observation. For six of them the observation was already committed and had never been graded against them, because the routes did not exist when the panel was built.' Its summary buckets are supported: 2, against: 3, withdrawn: 1, split_or_unread: 10. The paper's five are RT-ARGININE and RT-APOPTOSIS-DEP from 'against' plus RT-MDM2, RT-EZH2 and RT-POLQ from 'split_or_unread'; RT-MATRIX-SYNTHESIS, also graded 'against', is not in the paper. The manuscript's Summary reads 'We asked that question for five such classes, and for four of them the state is absent', with no statement that sixteen routes were graded against data already in hand or what rule selected these five. Separately, the panel reads themselves ARE pre-specified (artifact _limits: 'the reads were specified in advance'), and 156 group x platform scores were emitted in total - so the reported five classes draw on a small selected slice of a much larger set of computed contrasts.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: State the denominator: how many routes were graded against these readings, by what rule the five biomarker-selected classes were separated from the rest, and that the grading was done after the readings existed. One sentence in section 1 does it.

p2s.summary: BCL2L2, one of the five guardians the paper says are lower, is higher in EMC on GPL6244 at t = 2.908 - a larger |t| than the alt-EJ elevation the paper treats as a real finding.
p2s.evidence: gene_reads.BCL2L2 GPL6244: EMC mean_z 0.4786 vs comparator 0.3555, t = 2.908, signed_percentile 92.41; on GPL3290 it is lower (t = -0.351). The paper's sentence 'All five druggable guardians together are LOWER in EMC ... MCL1 and BCL2L1 individually included' is strictly accurate - the group score is lower and the two named genes are individually lower on both platforms (MCL1 1.981 vs 2.247 and -0.485 vs 0.072; BCL2L1 0.934 vs 1.314 and -0.640 vs -0.164, all verified) - but 'all five ... LOWER' will be read as five-for-five, and the reporting standard is inconsistent: t = 2.908 is not worth a mention here while t = 2.42 is a finding in section 2.4.

p2s.summary: The dependency-axis claim in section 2.5 gives a verbal quantifier where the artifact holds a number and an n.
p2s.evidence: Paper: 'MCL1 and BCL2L1 are dependencies in the large majority of sarcoma lines.' depmap-sarcoma-dependency.json, group 'Apoptotic guardians (BH3)': MCL1 sarcoma_frac_dependent = 0.835, BCL2L1 = 0.758, n_sarcoma = 91 for both; rest_frac_dependent 0.696 and 0.854 respectively. The verbal claim is correct but the paper prints neither fraction nor n, and it omits that BCL2L1 is LESS often dependent in sarcoma than in the rest of the panel (0.758 vs 0.854, selectivity -0.20) - which strengthens the paper's own anti-selectivity argument and costs nothing to state.

p2s.summary: The two-platform concordance argument compares non-identical gene sets in four of the five classes, and the paper never says so.
p2s.evidence: Per-platform genes_readable in emc-expression-panels.json: p53 transcriptional output 5/6 on GPL6244 (BBC3 unreadable) vs 6/6 on GPL3290; PRC2 core 4/4 vs 3/4 (SUZ12 unreadable); alt-EJ module 4/4 vs 3/4 (POLQ unreadable); homologous recombination 5/5 vs 4/5 (RAD52 unreadable); ncBAF 3/4 vs 2/4 (below the floor, no score). Only the guardian and NHEJ groups score the same members on both. 'On both platforms' therefore means 'on two overlapping but different gene sets against two different comparator arms'.

p2s.summary: The GPL3290 comparator arm is split across two different reference channels and two RNA preparations, confounded with histology - a real design feature the artifact's _limits do not mention. I tested whether it drives the results and it does not, for the genes I could check.
p2s.evidence: platforms['GSE4303-GPL3290...'].sample_annotations_verbatim: the ten EMC and three DFSP samples carry 'CRH' in the annotation while the three GIST samples carry 'UHR', and the GIST rows are 'Total RNA' where EMC and DFSP are 'mRNA'. The artifact's _limits describe GPL3290 as 'two-colour log-ratio against a reference pool', singular, and no code path splits the comparator arm. REFUTED as a driver by recomputation from gene_reads per_sample z values: ASS1 comparator subgroup means are DFSP/CRH -1.844 (n=3) and GIST/UHR -1.773 (n=3), against EMC -0.258; PMAIP1 are DFSP/CRH -1.998 (n=3) and GIST/UHR -1.918 (n=2), against EMC -0.222. The two reference channels agree closely, so the headline GPL3290 readings are not a reference-channel artefact. Worth one sentence as a stated-and-checked limitation rather than an unmentioned one.

_verdict_note: Not 'supported_with_reservations', because the failures land on the paper's own stated central contribution rather than around it. The Summary says 'the paper's central methodological claim is that saying [how strong each negative is] is the whole job', and the strength grading is precisely what does not survive: the artifact's own genome-wide empirical null puts |t| = 2.2 at an empirical two-sided p of 0.26-0.33, which removes the evidential basis for both readings the paper reports as PRESENT (alt-EJ, NOXA); the proliferation control the paper defers to falsifier F8 already exists and fails on GPL3290 (+1.24 SD, t = 2.30), so F8 is misstated as an open question; and one printed group definition ('29 comparator sarcomas') silently excludes five sarcomas from a 42-sample series through an unstated string match. Not 'needs_revision' as the recommendation either - major_revision, because none of this is fatal to the paper's thesis. The four negatives get STRONGER under the calibration finding, not weaker: a wider null makes an absent effect easier to defend. What has to go or be re-graded is the positive material and the strength language, and every fix above is a disclosure or a re-reading of data already committed - no new compute, no new fetch.
clean_checks: All fourteen t values quoted in section 2 match emc-expression-panels.json to the digit: p53 output -2.203/-1.126, PRC2 core -0.216/1.714, SWI/SNF -1.024/-0.083, alt-EJ 2.423/2.226, NHEJ -0.192/0.158, HR -0.573/1.035, guardians -4.568/-2.538.

Those figures are byte-stable across four artifact regenerations (generated_utc 2026-08-09, 2026-08-24 committed twice, 2026-08-29). The manuscript's last_verified date of 2026-08-09 predates three regenerations but no quoted number changed, so the figures are not stale.
ASS1's '92nd percentile' is the artifact's EMC mean_array_percentile 0.9152 on GPL6244 - correct.
NOXA's '1.74 standard deviations' on GPL3290 reproduces exactly: EMC mean_z -0.2219 minus comparator -1.9659 = 1.744.
MCL1 and BCL2L1 are individually lower in EMC on both platforms, as claimed.

The unit of analysis is the SAMPLE, not the gene: group scores are a within-sample mean z over readable members, then a Welch t across samples (emc_expression_panels.py _score_gene_list). Reported df of 5.4-20.1 are consistent with sample-level n. No pseudoreplication over genes.
The artifact refuses to emit a score below a coverage floor (3 genes and 0.5 coverage) rather than averaging over two probes, and the paper does not quote any UNDERPOWERED group as a number.
'An absent reading is not a reading of absence' is enforced in the code and honoured in the paper: no unreadable gene is reported as unexpressed anywhere.

Hypothesis tested and REFUTED: the GPL3290 comparator arm's split reference channel (CRH for DFSP, UHR for GIST) does not drive the ASS1 or NOXA results - the two subgroup means agree to within 0.08 SD in both cases.

Section 3 and section 5 do disclose that the analysis is uncorrected for multiple testing, that the comparator is other sarcoma, and that the dependency panel contains no EMC line. The disclosure is present; my blocker is that it names the wrong problem.
